body.statement:
For the saturated likelihood-ratio domain \(\mathcal V_P\), the full fixed-defect separated stratum \(\mathcal U_P\), and the actual path class in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{joint}}(P)\), does every \(s\in\mathcal C_P^\perp\) lie in the \(L^2(P)\)-closure of finite linear combinations of scores of admissible DQM paths, including at intersections with moving kernels and a shared \((W,X)\) marginal? Equivalently, does
\[
\mathcal T_P=\mathcal C_P^\perp
\]
hold on every such joint solvability germ?  Neither equality nor bridge-solvability path realization is included in the chart definition.
body.justification: This is the remaining reverse-inclusion problem for the repaired full path class.
body.gap: Finite constant-rank and branch calculations do not supply a general coupled Hilbert-space path lift.
body.consumer: Its resolution determines whether the general affine projection is the joint-model information bound.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove reverse score lifting on the full saturated fixed-defect joint solvability germ, including moving kernels and the shared marginal.
obligation.obstruction: Operator-norm continuity supplies continuous null projections but no local parameterization of the intersection of the two infinite-dimensional solvability loci. Linearized annihilation conditions alone do not realize actual dominated paths.
obligation.attempted: The singleton pathology was separated as a diagnostic. Exact positive finite checks were completed at the regular 36-cell law, the singular equal-arm two-branch law, and a positive 4-by-4 rank-two law with different arm row spaces. All three finite tangent spans agree with the proposed annihilator, but their finite coordinate charts do not extend to the general Hilbert germ.
obligation.partial_result: The forward algebraic normal family and three finite tests are established: at \(P^\star\), at the singular two-branch law \(P^\circ\), and at the transverse different-row-space law \(P^\square\), actual positive path scores span \(\mathcal C_P^\perp\).  For an arbitrary analyst-selected singleton chart the tangent is \(\{0\}\), proving that saturation is necessary.  What remains is the infinite-dimensional or unrestricted saturated-germ lifting theorem for the intersection of the two solvability loci.
